name_reason: Renamed ch29_major_cinematic -> ch29_yuni_endgame_trigger (category major_endgame_cinematic -> state_machine_mutator). The '_major_cinematic' label was wrong: this handler renders NO cinematic frames -- it shows dialog (page 0 or 1) and, for the designated trigger character char_id 9 = 悠妮/Yuni, arms the ch29 endgame turn-event chain (writes tile_event_data_table[+3] and [+6], primes handler_4A's 8-stage counter to 4). It is the character-gated LAUNCHER; the actual endgame cinematics are the armed handlers 0x4A/0x4C. Category state_machine_mutator matches the sibling turn-event armers (0x43/0x3E/0x41/0x45). '_4b' is the dispatch idx (entry @ 0x51CBD). ch29 walkthrough: 悠妮 must reach the stone tablet to trigger.
purpose: Chapter-29 endgame trigger tile (dispatch idx 0x4B, tile-step slot 1): when the designated character 悠妮 (Yuni, char_id 9) reaches the stone tablet and steps here, it launches the ch29 endgame turn-event sequence (arms hooks 0/1 + primes handler_4A's stage counter); any other non-enemy stepper gets a 'you're not the one' dialog and the tile stays armed. Renders no cinematic itself (the LAUNCHER, not the cinematic).
logic_summary: Tile-step ABI: stepping_char_id is the char that stepped on the tile. Gate: act only when the stepper is non-enemy (runtime_char_array[stepping_char].team != 0; encoding 0=enemy/1=npc/2=player) AND this slot is unconsumed (tile_event_consumed_flags[0x11] == 0). Inside the gate it branches on stepper char_id: (wrong char, char_id != 9) load the stepper's portrait, show in-frame dialog page 0 (render target 0xA951F), paint portrait, wait for input, close the status screen, and return WITHOUT consuming the slot so another character can retry. (right char, char_id == 9) show the full-screen page-1 cinematic dialog (render target 0xA0000), then perform four state mutations: consume this slot (tile_event_consumed_flags[0x11]=1), arm turn-event hook entry 1 for next turn (tile_event_data_table[+6]=(uint8)(turn_counter+1)), prime handler_4A's 8-stage counter to 4 (tile_event_consumed_flags[0x10]=4, skipping stages 0-3), and arm turn-event hook entry 0 for this turn (tile_event_data_table[+3]=(uint8)turn_counter). Both turn-counter stores are read as one byte; the +6 store is incremented in 8-bit (matches binary INC DL) and the +3 store is verbatim. The wrong-char path tail-calls fd2_close_status_screen_with_slide_out via JMP 0x196CB (binary size optimisation). __CHK(0x28) is the Watcom stack-probe prologue, no source semantics.

params.name: stepping_char_id
params.semantics: Index of the runtime char that stepped on the trigger tile (tile-step ABI, read from [ESP+0x4]). Used as the index into data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[] to read .team, .char_id and .portrait_id.
params.reason: Accurate (the stepping character id under the tile-step ABI), no address residue, matches the convention used by sibling tile-step handlers (handler_3a/3b/3c/3d use the same arg role).

returns.semantics: No return value. Falls through to RET in all paths (the wrong-char path returns early via a borrowed tail-call into fd2_close_status_screen_with_slide_out).

reads_globals: data_fd2_battle_turn_counter (0x53BEF; feeds both turn-event hook stores)
writes_globals: data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr[+6] = (uint8)(turn_counter+1) (arm turn-event hook entry 1, right-char path)
data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr[+3] = (uint8)turn_counter (arm turn-event hook entry 0, right-char path)
